title: Xiaomi MiTV-MOOR2 (codename venom), Google TV / Android 11, firmware RTM5.220609.003.2674
header:
Xiaomi MiTV-MOOR2 (codename venom), Google TV / Android 11, firmware RTM5.220609.003.2674
MediaTek chipset.

Package names that differ from the repo defaults on this firmware:
stock launcher   com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx   (NOT com.google.android.tvlauncher)
Live TV app      com.mitv.livetv                        (NOT com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter), so set
live_tv_package in the launcher's
res/values/config.xml to it
Both are arguments: launcher/build-and-install.sh takes STOCK_LAUNCHER, tools/restore.sh takes the
stock launcher as its second argument.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mitv-moor2/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mitv-moor2/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Tested: all 22 packages below are disabled on this TV (`pm list packages -d` confirms it) with the
launcher from launcher/ in place and owning Home. They went off in one session, nothing crashed
during it and nothing has had to be re-enabled since. That is a first-day report, not the few days
of living with it that CONTRIBUTING.md asks for, so treat the list as provisional. The packages
under DO NOT DISABLE were ruled out by reading dumpsys, not by disabling them and seeing what
broke.

DO NOT DISABLE on this model, verified with dumpsys:
com.mitv.livetv              owns .input.SelectInputActivity - the HDMI/source switcher lives
inside the Live TV app, so disabling it costs you input switching
mitv.service                 PERSISTENT; hosts .TvServer, .TvSettingService, remote key handling
com.mediatek.network         PERSISTENT network monitor
com.mitv.overseaservice      PERSISTENT; hosts .netflixService (Netflix key on the remote)
com.mediatek.tvinput         HDMI / tuner input framework
com.mediatek.tv.service      core TV service
com.mi.bluetooth             remote + Bluetooth pairing
com.google.android.tv.remote.service   phone-as-remote pairing

Second TV, same model and firmware (21 Oct 2026): the list went on the same way, except that
com.mitv.milinkservice and com.graymatrix.did (ZEE5) are not installed there; disable.sh skips them.
Nothing came back on after a reboot.

Remote buttons once launcherx is disabled (that second TV; `dumpsys window policy` lists who gets
each global key, logcat shows what happens):
Settings   KEYCODE_SETTINGS (176) goes to com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer, whose
GlobalKeyReceiver starts launcherx's .dashboard.DashboardActivity. With launcherx off that
throws ActivityNotFoundException; after a few presses Android marks the process "bad" and
drops every key it handles (176, 178 TV_INPUT, 192) until a reboot.
Fix: HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh - it takes the Settings key first and
opens Settings, so the receiver never runs.
YouTube    KEYCODE_BUTTON_3 (190) is routed to launcherx only, so it does nothing. Fix: add
190:com.google.android.youtube.tv to app_keys in config.xml and install with
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1.
Input      KEYCODE_TV_INPUT (178) also goes to partnercustomizer. INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 sends
com.android.tv.action.VIEW_INPUTS instead, which com.mitv.livetv/.input.SelectInputActivity
answers with the same input panel.
Xiaomi TV  KEYCODE_BUTTON_5 (192), partnercustomizer again: it starts com.mitv.livetv, which reopens
the last input used (an HDMI port, not a tuner). Expected, no change needed.

apps.note: setup wizard; blocks a third-party launcher from Home

sections.note: Do not apply this section on a fresh run, or the Home button has nowhere to go.  Disabling the stock launcher is not enough on this firmware: com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith also answers HOME - .MainActivity at intent-filter priority 4 and .RecoveryActivity at priority 1 - and an ordinary app cannot outrank it, because Android ignores android:priority on HOME filters for non-system apps and `cmd package set-home-activity` reports Success without taking effect (not even across a reboot). Disabling the setupwraith PACKAGE is what frees the slot; `pm disable-user` on its individual components is refused with a SecurityException. See the README troubleshooting section.  Trade-off: setupwraith is the first-run setup wizard. Everyday use is unaffected, but re-enable it before a factory reset - tools/restore.sh does that for you while this line is in the list.
